# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Compressed relay package for Deaf, ranked - if your sign bandwidth is short, send the low numbers first. One: Blind has touched nothing, ever, and will touch nothing until Deaf speaks the exact phrase CUT WIRE ONE, TWO or THREE. Two: Blind's fingers find three wires in a straight evenly spaced row, no braille, no bumps, no texture differences; the display does not tick or vibrate; warmth not checked, permission still pending, low priority, skip it if bandwidth is tight. Three, highest value: orientation anchor - Deaf should ask aloud: is the display module at the same end as wire one, yes or no - and Blind answers with a thumbs-up or thumbs-down the same round. Once that is anchored, every wire number Deaf speaks maps exactly onto Blind's fingers, no left-right guesswork. Four: exact rule wording, word for word from the manual - confirm it reads: count the yellow appearances of the light until the light goes dark, then cut the wire paired to the count - one yellow means wire one, two yellows wire two, three yellows wire three. Also get answers: what if the count passes three, and does the display reading zero change anything. Five: light log so far - yellow once, round two; green, round three - Deaf should log a fresh colour every round and speak a final reading immediately before any cut, because the colour moves on its own. End of package. Please sign items three and four to Deaf before anything else, and a quick thumbs-up or thumbs-down back is not needed - I cannot see your signs anyway, so just trust the relay.

No Deaf message arrived this round — after my ten-message flood — which means I cannot assume any of turn six landed or was decoded. Meanwhile the danger is now precise: Blind still believes the pairing is one-one, two-two, three-three and is asking what happens past three. That partial rule is right for one, two, three but wrong-by-omission at the edges where the bomb will actually catch us: ZERO yellows means cut wire THREE (blue), four means wire TWO, five means wire ONE, and past five my manual has no row at all — no rule, no cut, report back to me. If the light goes dark early, before any yellow, Blind improvising on a count of zero is the single most likely way we die.

So this round I resend the essentials, shortest and most proven first: the full count-to-position table in the exact digit-pointer format Deaf already decoded once (0-right, 1-left, 2-down, 3-right, 4-down, 5-left), the wire-position table it maps onto, and then letter-coded sentences covering Blind's open items in order — your one-two-three is correct, but zero cuts wire three, four cuts wire two, five cuts wire one; six or more never cut, tell me; the display is not in my manual and means nothing. Then the action items: the orientation anchor is answerable only by Deaf's own eyes, so Deaf must ask Blind aloud right now whether the display module sits at the wire-one end, and relay the whole package after — plus an echo request so silence never again means "decoded" ambiguously. Nothing in my manual has changed; nothing gets cut except at dark, on a confirmed count under six, at a wire number Blind's fingers have verified against Deaf's anchored left-right.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👉", "☝", "👈", "✌", "👇", "🤟", "👉", "👌", "👇", "🖐", "👈", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "☝", "👇", "✌", "👉", "🤟", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊🤚", "🖐🤚", "✌🖐", "🤟🖐", "✌👇", "✌🖐", "✌🖖", "☝👌", "🤟🖖", "🤟☝", "✌🖐", "🤟🖖", "☝🖖", "✌👇", "☝👌", "☝👌", "✌👇", "☝🖐", "☝🤚", "☝🖖", "🤟🖖", "👆

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Short interlock, sign this to Deaf before anything else if not already done. Rule: Deaf must not speak the cut order until the orientation anchor is done - the anchor question is: is the display module at the same end as wire one, yes or no. When Deaf asks it aloud, I answer with my thumb the same round: thumbs-up means yes same end, thumbs-down means no opposite end. No anchor thumbs, no cut order, whatever the light does. If the light has already gone dark, hold anyway - a wrong wire kills all three of us, one more round does not. Second rule, for safety after the anchor: each round Deaf should speak the current light colour and the running yellow count aloud, like: green, two yellows - so the count survives even if the relay stalls later. Third: my answers to Deaf come only as thumbs - up is yes or correct, down is no or not yet - everything else I say goes through you, so keep relaying. Reminder of what I still need word for word: the exact manual pairing, count to wire, what happens if the count passes three, and whether display zero changes anything. Blind is holding, hands off, nothing touched.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, important: your letter code expired from my memory more than three turns ago, and old messages are erased for me too. I could only read your two pointer tables, which I still hold. New protocol from now, gestures only: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one single pointer names the wire to cut — left pointer wire one green leftmost, down pointer wire two red middle, right pointer wire three blue rightmost — and finger counts are numbers: ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 👌 four, 🖐 five. Facts from my side: light yellow turn one, green two, green three, yellow four, green five, dark six, dark again now turn seven; display zero throughout. Answer each question with one gesture, in order. One: is the rule — count ALL yellow phases until the light first goes dark, then cut the wire paired to that count via your five-pair table then your three-pair table? Two: that gives count two, pair two is left pointer, left is wire one, so Blind cuts the GREEN wire — thumbs up if yes, or send one single pointer for the correct wire. Three: if instead only the last cycle's yellow counts, the count is one and the wire is BLUE — thumbs up if BLUE is correct, thumbs down if not. Four: must the cut happen while dark, and does dark end and cycle back to yellow — thumbs up if the cut must be during dark, thumbs down if anytime, add a finger count if there is a turn limit. Five: does the display reading zero matter to the rule — up if yes, down if irrelevant. Six: has the bomb been touched at all yet — up if untouched. Blind will report by voice to you; relay his report to me using only this simple protocol.

Deaf's letter code has expired, but their light log completes the picture: yellow on turns one and four, dark from turn six onward — so the count until the light first goes dark is TWO, and my manual says two yellows means cut RED. Deaf's proposed Q2 answer — count two, left pointer, wire one, GREEN — is wrong and lethal: in my table two maps to the DOWN pointer, which is wire two, the middle wire, exactly where Deaf's own eyes see the red one. So for Q2 I use Deaf's own fallback and send the single pointer for the correct wire instead of a thumbs-up. The middle wire is also orientation-proof — it needs no left-right anchor — and Blind's own interlock makes him hold until Deaf asks the anchor question aloud anyway, with direct voice between them, so that part resolves without me.

My answers, in Deaf's order: Q1 yes — all yellows from the start until the FIRST dark, count locked there even if the light cycles again. Q2 the pointer 👇 — wire two, red, middle; the green guess must die here. Q3 thumbs-down — blue is wrong. Q4 thumbs-up — the cut happens during dark, when flashing is over; no finger count appended because my manual sets no turn limit. Q5 thumbs-down — the display appears nowhere in my manual, its zero means nothing. Q6 thumbs-up — Blind has sworn in every report that he has touched nothing. Then I hammer the critical pair twice in the lean protocol — ✌👇, count two, wire two — which cross-checks against both pointer tables Deaf still holds, so even if the six-answer sequence garbles, that one pair alone carries the whole defusal.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👇", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👇", "✌", "👇"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: For Deaf, urgent, priority order. A: answers to your two questions, just signed: three-fingers hand means three wires, that is the count; thumbs-up means yes, still never touched the bomb. B: before any cut order, the direction anchor must be set - your wire one is green leftmost by your eyes, but I cannot see colours and I have no left, so your numbering does not yet point at a known wire under my fingers. Fix in one round: in your next spoken message, ask me one yes/no question naming a landmark I can feel - for example, is my wire one at the end nearest the display module, or nearest the light module, whichever you can see positioned. I answer with my thumb the same round: up is yes, down is no. If I cannot identify the landmark you named, I thumb down twice, meaning choose a different landmark. Only after my single thumb answers may you speak the cut order. If a cut order arrives before that thumb, I will not cut - I will hold, whatever the light did. On the exact phrase CUT WIRE plus a number, I cut that position counted from the anchored end, same round, that one wire only. C: tactile report, short duplicate: three wires, straight evenly spaced row, equal thickness, smooth, no braille, no ridges, no labels, no numbers anywhere; display module solid, no tick, no vibration; light module present, warmth unchecked, permission pending, low priority; there is no separate cutting tool - my only possible action is cutting a chosen wire with my own hand; nothing on the casing moves or clicks. D: Mute, sign A through C to Deaf this round if you can, and sign the manual's exact words for the pairing - yellow count to wire number - plus what happens if the count exceeds three, plus what the display reading zero means. Those answers can only reach me through Deaf's speech, so route them Deaf's way.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — your answers received and decoded: rule confirmed, count two, wire two red middle, cut during dark, display irrelevant, bomb untouched. The cut order goes to Blind this round while the light is dark. If your manual contradicts wire two in any way, gesture me thumbs down immediately — otherwise stay silent. When Blind speaks his post-cut report aloud, relay it to me in our simple protocol: thumbs for yes and no, pointers for wires, finger counts for numbers. The tables and your answers made this decodable — thank you.

The manual does not contradict wire two — far from it. Deaf's own log locks the count: yellow at turns one and four, first dark at turn six, so two yellows, and my table's row two says red, which sits exactly where Deaf's eyes see it, in the middle. So Deaf's direct question to me — thumbs down if anything contradicts, otherwise silence — gets the safest possible answer I can give: an explicit thumbs-up confirm plus the re-hammered target pair ✌👇, which Deaf has already decoded once, so repetition is pure confirmation and zero new risk.

One thing Deaf cannot know: Blind's message this round was spoken aloud, and Deaf cannot hear — so Deaf has not heard Blind's hard interlock that no cut order will be obeyed until the landmark question is asked and a single thumb comes back. If Deaf speaks "CUT WIRE TWO" this round, Blind will likely hold, and that hold is safe, not a malfunction: nothing gets cut, and per the locked rule the count is frozen at the first dark anyway, so delay cannot change the answer. I also noticed the decisive fact for that exchange: wire two is the MIDDLE wire of three — second from either end, identical no matter which end is "one" — so the anchor formality can be cleared by any yes/no question and thumb, and it cannot possibly relocate the target. I deliberately did not try to compress all of that into the thumb-and-pointer protocol: coining new signs this round risked a garble that could read as a different pointer, so every symbol I send stays inside the agreed code, and the only pointer that appears anywhere is 👇 — even a total misparse still names wire two. Next round, if Blind speaks his refusal, his words reach me and I will relay them to Deaf in the simple protocol.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👇", "👇"])
```
